questions.history: On the merge record the four-argument onRetryFailure and onRetrySuccess callbacks during E0, E1, R.
questions.prediction: Parent lacks these overloads. On the merge expect one failure callback for E1 with count 1 and exceptions [E0,E1], then one success callback for R with count 2 and the same exception sequence. execute returns R.
questions.basis: RetryState defines zero as the initial attempt. E0 initiates retries, E1 fails retry one, and R succeeds on retry two.
questions.refutation: A failure callback is emitted for E0, a count/history is wrong, or the returned result differs from the success callback’s result.

questions.history: For the same retry history install a listener overriding only the older three-argument callbacks. Then execute an immediately successful operation.
questions.prediction: Both revisions should deliver failure E1 and success R once for the first operation. Initial success in the second should produce neither retry callback.
questions.basis: The callbacks describe retry attempts. Default overload delegation promises compatibility for existing implementations.
questions.refutation: The legacy listener misses or duplicates an event or reports a retry for an initial success.

questions.history: Put one legacy listener and one state-aware listener into CompositeRetryListener and install it on the merged template.
questions.prediction: Both should see E1 then R once. The state-aware listener should observe counts 1 then 2, regardless of its position in the composite.
questions.basis: Fan-out must preserve the argument each delegate elected to receive. Per-delegate records catch missing forwarding.
questions.refutation: A delegate sees an extra event, misses a callback, or reads count zero on success.

questions.history: With a composite holding just the legacy listener, directly call its public three-argument onRetryFailure and onRetrySuccess with E1 and R, as a pre-existing caller can.
questions.prediction: Parent forwards both to the listener. Preservation would forward them on the merge too. The landed composite overrides only the four-argument forms, predicting that both direct calls silently do nothing.
questions.basis: The same public receiver, method signatures, arguments and recording listener are available in both revisions.
questions.refutation: Empty delegate history on the merge refutes compatibility even if every RetryTemplate-driven assertion passes.
